anomalies.observed: R36 is given value "24k", but its own library and MPN fields describe a 24 ohm part (FRC0805J240TSD, "24Ω 0805"). The SPICE deck also models it as 24k.
anomalies.expected: A 24 ohm part, matching the MPN and description, if the 24k value is a typo. The netlist value is internally inconsistent, so either the value or the part is wrong.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R36") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: A 1000x error in a resistor across the high-voltage output rail would change its current draw and dissipation. At 24 ohm across the bank it would dissipate far more than its 125 mW rating, while at 24k it would act as a bleed. Either way the rail's loading behaves differently from the intended design.

anomalies.observed: Channel 2 of the dual LED D30 has its anode A2 (pin 4) on ESTOP_OUT, and its cathode K2 (pin 2) goes through R60 to ESTOP_OUT as well. Both ends of the LED sit on the same net, so it has no voltage across it and cannot light. Channel 1 is wired as anode-to-supply and cathode-via-R59-to-GND.
anomalies.expected: The second LED channel should have its cathode return to GND through R60, mirroring channel 1 (R59 to GND). Its anode should be driven from a supply or indicator net, not from ESTOP_OUT on both sides.
anomalies.impact: The e-stop indicator LED channel driven from ESTOP_OUT would never light, so the operator would get no visual confirmation of that e-stop state. The fault is in the indicator only, not the e-stop loop itself.
